pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
At Strand on the Green Infant and Nursery School, we place children at the heart of what we do, cherishing and inspiring them all with an active, engaging, and stimulating curriculum. Our highly experienced and committed staff work hard, in partnership with parents, to ensure every child can experience success. We are proud to be an inclusive school that meets the needs of all learners. We have the highest expectations for behaviour and learning right from the start.
As an Infant school, we are able to capitalise on our expertise in teaching very young children, using pedagogy that suits our young learners. Whilst our focus is on the fundamentals of language aquisition, reading, writing, and arithmetic, this is taught alongside a very creative and broad, active curriculum. Children learn how to work and play together, be healthy, use their imaginations and be creative; all of which develops a love of learning, curiosity, and fun. When the time comes, it is then a smooth and easy transfer to our linked Junior school next door.
We are uniquely situated, tucked away in Strand on the Green within a stone’s throw of the River Thames. Our children love to learn inside and out using our pond, field, sensory garden and our Forest School areas.
If you have visited our school already you will know that children, staff, parents and governors together create a warm, vibrant and welcoming community that is second to none. If you haven’t visited us yet, book a place on one of our regular tours (via the school office) and come and meet us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission Statement and Values - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
Our Mission
At Strand on the Green Infant and Nursery School, our mission will always be to ‘Cherish and inspire every child’
Our Vision and Rationale
Our vision is that all children make excellent academic progress, no matter their starting point, developing and maintaining great physical well-being and mental health. We want them to leave our school, ready for the Junior School, with positive attitudes to learning, feeling confident and enjoying good relationships.
This excellent foundation will enable all of our children to become well rounded individuals, successful and happy in life, eventually contributing to a rapidly evolving world, changing things for the better.
Our Golden Values
These are the principles and beliefs that underpin everything we do in school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum and Pedagogy in the Swan Centre - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
In the Swan Centre, we provide an ambitious, autism-specialist curriculum that aims to help every child make excellent progress from their individual starting points.
Our focus is on developing academic skills alongside developing communication, social skills, independence and emotional regulation so that pupils are well prepared for the next stages of their education and life. We draw on TEACCH principles, the EQUALS curriculum, and an adapted National Curriculum to ensure learning is structured, meaningful, and accessible for all.
We use clear TEACCH structure, with individual visual schedules, small-group teaching, visual supports, and predictable routines to help pupils feel secure and ready to learn. Pupils follow an adapted version of the National curriculum combined with elements from the EQUALS curriculum. Pupils benefit from integrated support from Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, and sensory regulation tools. Communication, social interaction, and emotional regulation are taught explicitly using approaches such as AAC systems and the Zones of Regulation. Learning is broken into manageable steps, with a focus on repetition and overlearning to embed skills and is tailored to each child’s needs and EHCP outcomes.
As a result, pupils make strong and meaningful progress in academic skills as well as communication, social understanding, independence, and emotional regulation. They become more confident, better able to manage their emotions and routines, and increasingly independent in daily tasks. Pupils leave the Swan centre well equipped for the next stage of their education, with the skills and strategies they need to thrive in life.
We make sure our learning is real, meaningful and concrete, with a focus on real life skills, including regular trips into the local community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pelican Music Provision - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
We employ talented and enthusiastic music teachers from an external provider, Pelican Music.
If you are unable to pay for Pelican Music, are eligible for benefit related free school meals and feel that your child would benefit from music tuition please contact the school office as we may be able to support with a subsidised place.
Students can learn an instrument right from Reception.
Reception - Violin and Cello
Year 1 - Violin, Cello, Guitar, Woodwind, and Piano
Year 2 - Violin, Cello, Piano, Woodwind, Brass, and Drums
Interested in Your Child Learning at Strand on the Green Infants?
If you have any questions, or would like to apply for lessons, you can call or email us on:

pageCache.pageTitle: Parents Association (Friends of Strand Schools) - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
Friends of Strand Schools is our Parent Teacher Association (PTA), of which all parents and carers are automatically members. Friends is a registered charity and consists of a group of dedicated volunteer Strand parents who work alongside the staff of both the Infant and Junior schools to organise community events and raise much needed extra funds for the schools. Every penny raised goes directly to the schools to enrich and enhance the children’s school experience.
Over the years Friends has raised funds for many additional items including a class set of Chromebooks, a new climbing frame in the playground, redevelopment of outdoor areas, floodlights, sports equipment, outdoor equipment and renovations to areas of the schools.
The main annual events are:
Fireworks (November)
Christmas Fair (December)
Bingo & Curry Night (January)
Other fundraising initiatives run throughout the year for example, the Wish List launched in January 2024 to support the exciting redevelopment of the field.
In order for the events and fundraising to be as successful as possible Friends needs as much help as possible from parents/carers, so if you are interested in helping out whether it be putting up posters, selling tickets, sourcing raffle/auction prizes, helping out at an event or offering fundraising ideas or expertise, Friends would love to hear from you. Your support means the world to us and our schools and we cannot do it without you all!
Please contact Friends at friendsofstrandschools@gmail.com

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading Passports - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
The Strand Infants Reading Passport
We have carefully considered books for each year group and produced a list to encourage children to enjoy a range of high quality reading. Children receive rewards as they read more on the list.
Books are available for change daily at year group pick up or drop off points. We ask that books are borrowed and then returned for others to borrow. To help us maintain a healthy number of books available to you we collect donations for books at our termly poetry recitals and belong to book schemes such as 'WeBuyBooks'.

pageCache.pageTitle: Before and After School Care - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
Extended Nurture Club (after school care for Nursery and Reception pupils)
Extended Nurture Club is managed by the Infant school and run by existing school staff. This provision is open to Nursery and Reception children only.
Children will be offered a variety of Early Years play opportunities during the week including the Forest and outdoor learning areas, with the Thames Nurture Room as their base. Children are offered a substantial healthy snack.
Sessions cost £13.50 and run from 3.25pm until 5.45pm.
We endeavour to meet demand and ask that parents apply for places as early as possible to help us help you (as soon as you are offered a school place). Please enquire via the School Office or see the documents shared below for more information and a registration form.
02089947921communications@strandin.hounslow.sch.uk
After School Care Parents Handbook
Extended Nurture Club Payment Terms and ConditionsExtended Nurture Club Registration Form
Introduction Letter to Reception and Nursery Parents
Cygnet Club (before and after school care for Reception through to Year 6)
Cygnet Club is a breakfast and after-school club managed and situated in our linked Junior school. There are a limited number of Reception places and more provision from Year 1 upwards.
Children are offered a variety of play opportunities in the Cygnet Club rooms and the playground within the Junior School. Children are offered a light meal.
Places are limited due to Ofsted regulations and parents/carers are strongly advised to apply for a place as early as possible. Please click on the link below to access information about Cygnet Club via the Strand on the Green Junior School website.

All children attending our school will have access to the following digital resources to support their learning, the links below will take you to their login pages;
Online Safety
Along with the many benefits that online digital technologies bring to learning there are also many risks. As a school we have a responsibility to educate our pupils to stay safe when operating within online environments and working in partnership with parents is the only way this can be truly effective due to the nature of this being such an integrated home and school resource.
Online safety is embedded within both the Computing and RSE curriculums and drip fed to children throughout every school year to keep it present in their thinking. Individuals use a variety of online resources therefore their needs in terms of online safety can be very different; as well as communications sent home, the links provided below are excellent in providing information and guidance for both teachers in schools and parents at home. In addition school staff receive regular training regarding online safety and are available to support you with any particular concerns.
Please open the links below to access further advice on how to stay 'safe online' at home;

pageCache.pageTitle: About the Swan Centre - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
The Swan Centre is a unit within our mainstream school that caters for children with Autism. We provide children with opportunities to really thrive, to learn with the highest of expectations, and to make the most of their skills and talents. Emphasis is given to developing life skills with a tailored curriculum for students to focus on their communication, independence and social interaction skills.
The Swan Centre is about 'promoting inclusiveness in a way that is special and individual to every child' - Quote from parent.
The Swan Centre is made up of three classes: Kingfisher (Reception and Years 1 and 2), Otter (Year 3 and 4) and River (Year 5 and Year 6).
The leadership, governance and funding of the centre is shared between the Infant and the Junior School.
All the pupils in the Swan Centre have a diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Condition (ASC) and an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP).
Children learn in a smaller class size in their own classroom with specially trained practitioners. They also benefit from integration with mainstream with an approach tailored by year group and bespoke to individuals.
The Centre also has a Sensory Room and an Outdoor Learning Area.
What we can offer your child
The Swan Centre is designed to meet the needs of children who would benefit from time in a mainstream classroom as well as the structure of the specialised learning environment we offer in Kingfisher, Otter and River Class. Consequently, integration into the main school is part of our offer to families.
We take a bespoke and tailored approach to integration and the amount of time spent in mainstream varies by child, by year group and by the time of year.
All pupils integrate for lunch times and playtimes.
We have a Speech and Language therapist who works one day a week across the Centre. She works with pupils 1:1 or in small group sessions. We also have a Occupational Therapist who works one day a week with the pupils to address fine and gross motor skills or any sensory issues. We have a linked Educational Psychologist to support practitioners.
Communication with parents and carers
As many pupils come to school on transport, communication with parents happens daily via our home learning platform Seesaw. In addition, parents/carers are encouraged to visit the Centre or to telephone staff at any time. Each child has a termly Individual Education Plan, an Annual Review meeting is held to review the EHCP and progress towards longer term outcomes. Parents also receive a weekly curriculum letter outlining the learning that is happening in class and suggestions for ideas to support your child with further learning at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
Our Nursery and our Reception classes follow the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework, supported by the non-statutory Development Matters. The EYFS educational programmes provide us with the curriculum framework which is then built upon further to decide the wider learning content that best fits the interests and needs of our children. The curriculum is sequential, taking small steps and then broadening and deepening learning across a wide range of experiences.
Language development within a language rich environment is at the absolute heart of our curriculum with indoor and outdoor learning environments being carefully planned to stimulate and enable conversation. Children learn through play and careful modelling from adults and they develop problem solving skills in response to bouncing back from challenges. Where possible our children are given the opportunity to learn through first hand experiences, such as growing their own herbs to utilise in real and imaginary cooking scenarios, and exploring life cycles through real chicks and ducks hatching in their classrooms.
Children receive feedback whilst they learn as practitioners praise what went well, share why they were successful and comment on what they could improve. Their 'in school' learning journey is shared with parents and carers through a mixture of video, photos and written information using the Google learning platform 'Seesaw'. Parents are encouraged to add to this by also uploading and sharing experiences and learning successes from home.

RE in the EYFS
Religious Education is statutory for all pupils registered on the school role. While it is not statutory in Nursery, we very much see its value in the educational experience of our children and follow the recommendations in the Hounslow Borough RE syllabus, Widening Horizons. Religious education in the EYFS makes particularly important contributions to the following areas of learning and development in the EYFS curriculum: PSED, CLL, UtW and EAD. Exploring Religious Education through the EYFS will give children the chance to reflect on their own thoughts and experiences and to be curious about the word in which they live.
Parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all parts of Religious Education. Before making a decision to withdraw, we always encourage parents and carers to come into school and speak to a senior leader.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Session Options  - Strand on the Green
pageCache.text:
15 Hour offer
All 3 and 4 year old children are entitled to attend Nursery for 15 hours per week. We offer either 15 hour morning or 15 hour afternoon places;
Morning Nursery 8.45am-11.45am
Afternoon Nursery 12.50pm-3.50pm
30 Hour Offer
Some children will be eligible for an additional 15 hours funding, giving a total of 30 hours per week. Our 30 hour per week offer gives families 4.5 days of provision. The remaining morning/ afternoon session can be paid for by parents directly with the school.
You may be eligible if
If you believe you are eligible you must obtain an eligibility code. Full details on eligibility and how to apply can be found by following this link 30 hours free childcare - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)/
Your eligibility code must then be shared with the school before you can be offered 30 hours, 30 hour places are subject to spaces being available.
Additional privately paid sessions
If you are not eligible for 30 hours of Government funded provision then you may purchase additional Nursery sessions directly with us, subject to space being available. This is usually agreed and paid for in advance of each term. Currently, fees are £10.00 for each lunch session only or £35.00 for a lunch and afternoon session together.
Lunch session 11.45am-12.50pm
Afternoon Nursery 12.50pm-3.50pm
You will be asked to request anticipated additional sessions on application to help us plan provision and staffing. It is also possible to pay for ad hoc additional sessions dependent on availability.
Extended Nurture Club - After Care
You may also book after school care for your Nursery child. The fee is currently £13.50 and this includes a healthy snack. Please register and book using the information and forms in your welcome pack or via the school office,
After school session 3.50-5.45pm
